avertissement: Traductions automatiques des textes français ; chaque nombre a été vérifié contre le français. Les documents de la Ville sont en français et font foi.

canopee.description: Tree planting, greening, fighting the emerald ash borer and heat islands.
canopee.enBref: This year, the City is paying companies to plant and maintain trees on streets and in parks, and it is funding an organization that plants on private and institutional land. Boroughs are adding their own money, machinery and employee teams to plant trees. Two boroughs also allowed construction projects to deviate from the rules on trees and greening.

etapes.titre: Contracts to plant trees on streets
etapes.texte: City council awards two contracts to 7574479 Canada inc. and Terrassement Technique Sylvain Labrecque inc. to supply and plant 1,374 trees on public land, then water, maintain and replace some of them. The authorized expense is $2,456,590.55, taxes included, and the trees go to seven boroughs, including Saint-Laurent (423), Verdun (281) and Pierrefonds-Roxboro (265).

etapes.titre: Money to plant on private property
etapes.texte: The City pays $3,071,550 to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain to plant and maintain trees on private and institutional sites from March 24 to December 31, 2026. The organization and its Alliance forêt urbaine partners must plant 14,500 trees and 2,500 shrubs in 2026.

Pierrefonds-Roxboro transfers up to $162,233.12 from its parks fund to buy trees and plants. Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve rents a mini-backhoe with an operator for $152,916.75 and sets aside $200,000 for additional blue-collar worker teams, with a target of about 1,000 trees planted in 2026.

etapes.titre: Two exceptions to the tree rules
etapes.texte: Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve allows a company to expand its building at 1620, rue Préfontaine with 25 trees and 5% greening, instead of the required 40 trees and 25%, with the company offsetting this on its other lots. Montréal-Nord allows trees to be planted less than 1.5 metres from the street line at 5745, boulevard Léger, for a two-storey building.

etapes.titre: Work at parc Pratt, in Outremont
etapes.texte: Outremont awards URBEX CONSTRUCTION INC. the renovation of the parc Pratt chalet and the redevelopment of its surroundings, including planting vegetation, water retention and new paths. The authorized expense is $800,416.17, taxes included, funded mostly by the Programme de réfection et de verdissement des parcs locaux.

aSurveiller.texte: The Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain must submit progress reports on July 31 and October 31, 2026, its accountability report by December 31, 2026 at the latest, then its report and financial statements on March 31, 2027.
Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve's tree planting takes place from April or May to November 2026.
Watering, maintenance and replacement of trees planted under the central city contract continue until the end of November 2029.

deneigement.description: Snow removal and snow loading contracts, spreading of abrasives, parking by-laws.

etapes.titre: Rental of sweepers and sidewalk washers
etapes.texte: Boroughs are renting vacuum sweepers, tanker trucks, sidewalk washers and a mini sweeper with operators to clean streets, lanes, sidewalks and bike paths in the spring. Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is authorizing an expenditure of $574,920.99, taxes included, for four vacuum sweepers and three tanker trucks [CA26 27 0008].

etapes.titre: Snow removal for downtown public squares
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie is entrusting companies with the maintenance, cleanliness and snow removal of square Viger, place des Montréalaises and six squares including square Dorchester and square Victoria. The borough is also extending snow removal for the Quartier des Spectacles by one year, from April 2, 2026 to April 1, 2027 [CA26 24 0067].

etapes.titre: Staff for Verdun's snow disposal site
etapes.texte: Verdun is offering city council to provide the staff for the snow disposal site itself during loading operations, for 2025, 2026 and 2027. The positions concerned are gatehouse attendants, sewer chute supervisors and drivers and operators.

Montréal-Nord is approving an additional expenditure of $106,150.97, taxes included, for the rental of a grader with operator [CA26 10 086]. Saint-Léonard is drawing $200,000 from its surpluses to pay for staff and abrasives [CA26 13 0121].

aSurveiller.texte: Saint-Léonard indicates that the adoption of its snow removal by-law is scheduled for September 8, 2026, with a notice of coming into force on September 9, 2026.
The extended towing contracts start on November 15, 2026.
The rental of equipment with operator in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie resumes on November 1, 2026 and runs until March 31, 2027.
The extension of the grader rental contract in Anjou covers November 15, 2026 to April 15, 2027.

eau-egouts.description: Pipes, drinking water production plants, Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, retention basins.

etapes.texte: The City is raising the loan for the disinfection unit at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant from $197,000,000 to $381,000,000. The money is to be used to finish the ozonation unit, install liquid oxygen tanks and build the oxygen plant.

The City is awarding contracts to FER-PAL Construction and Services d'infrastructures Vortex to rehabilitate secondary water pipes without trenching and redo the roadway, on streets in more than a dozen boroughs. These projects include replacing lead water service connections on both the public and private sides.

The City is awarding Pronex Excavation the reconstruction of a 500 mm water pipe on rue Guy, and Les Entreprises Michaudville work on rue De Champlain, where a 1,200 mm pipe installed in 1927 is being replaced. It is adding $12,144,522.14 in contingencies to Pomerleau's contract for the rue de la Cathédrale pipe, after an inspection revealed more damaged sections than in 2019.

aSurveiller.texte: Commissioning of the ozone plant at the Jean-R.-Marcotte plant expected in 2029; contracts for lots 4, 5 and 6 must be completed by the last quarter of 2028.
Completion of work on the rue de la Cathédrale pipe pushed back from December 2026 to March 2027.
Leak detection on main pipes: work from July 2026 to June 2028.
Rehabilitation of the 600 mm pipe along autoroute 15 Nord: work starting in September 2026, to be completed by December 18, 2026 at the latest.
Rue Guy project expected from the second quarter of 2026 to December 2027.
Federal grant of up to $128.3M conditional on completing infrastructure by 2031 in the Namur–De la Savane sector.

frederic-back.titre: Parc Frédéric-Back and Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel
frederic-back.description: The former quarry turned dump, transformed into a park in phases: urban greenhouses, biogas capture, and electrical system upgrades.
frederic-back.enBref: This year, the City is moving forward on three fronts at parc Frédéric-Back and the Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel: a greenhouse complex in the Saint-Michel neighbourhood, the modernization of electrical installations linked to biogas capture, and park maintenance. It is also requesting financial help from Québec for an east-west pedestrian and bike link with a footbridge. At the same time, the borough is redeveloping rue De Louvain, along the edge of the park.

etapes.titre: Funding request for the east-west link
etapes.texte: The City is asking the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable du Québec for help of up to $2,000,000 for a 900-metre trail crossing the park from east to west, including a footbridge about 150 metres long (CG26 0121). The project also includes stormwater management works and a 12.7-hectare meadow.

The agglomeration approves the construction of a research, training and community production greenhouse complex, valued at $2,185,000, then delegates the project to city council (CG26 0124). The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension offers to carry it out and city council accepts (CA26 14 0039, CM26 0363).

The City awards Systèmes Urbains inc. a contract worth $1,091,693.37, taxes included, for the second phase of electrical work at the Complexe environnemental de Saint-Michel, which includes a new 25 kV power supply, a backup generator and an automated controller to manage biogas capture (CG26 0223). It also entrusts two companies with the park's general upkeep and ecological and horticultural management for 30 months (CG26 0224).

The borough awards Groupe MPotvin the redevelopment of rue De Louvain, between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum amount of $8,199,514.82, taxes included, and authorizes total spending of $11,192,464.62. The work covers sewers and water mains, lighting, traffic lights, sidewalks, the bike path and plantings.

The City extends the rental of a compost screener and a loader tractor with operator at the Complexe environnemental de Saint-Michel by five months, for an additional $296,349.21, taxes included. The compost, made from leaves collected in parks and streets, is used in particular for the landscaping of parc Frédéric-Back (CG26 0320).

The borough awards Les industries Harnois inc. the supply and installation of the greenhouse complex, for a maximum amount of $499,865.92, taxes included, and authorizes total spending of $574,845.80. The project covers two greenhouses with structure, envelope, natural ventilation, ground surfaces, interior partitions and condensation water management.

aSurveiller.texte: Greenhouses: infrastructure delivery in July 2026, work starting in August 2026 and expected completion in December 2026, according to the borough's file.
Greenhouses expected to be in service by winter 2027.
The call for projects under the ministère des Transports' assistance program, for the footbridge and east-west link, ends on November 26, 2026.
Rue De Louvain: work in three phases, from May to November 2026, from May to October 2027, then from May to August 2028.
Park maintenance: contracts from May 1, 2026 to October 31, 2028; 26 hectares will be added to the park in 2027 in the Boisé Ouest sector.
Rental of the screener and loader tractor from June 20 to October 15, 2026.

grand-parc-ouest.description: Canada's largest municipal park, being assembled: land acquisitions, Anse-à-l'Orme, Cap-Saint-Jacques, Bois-de-la-Roche, parc-nature des Sources.

etapes.titre: More money for the stone walls
etapes.texte: The City is adding $162,897.98 to the contract with Les Constructions H2D inc. to redo heritage walls along chemin de Senneville, bringing the contract to $1,174,331.77. According to the file, buried stones, surplus mortar and a deteriorated culvert explain the increase; the work, 60% complete as of December 1, 2025, resumes on May 15, 2026.

The City is submitting an application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector, described as covering 330 hectares, for the international Urban Night Sky Place designation from DarkSky International. The application involves no spending; the City commits to producing a lighting management plan, bringing its light fixtures up to standard and keeping the site accessible in the evening.

etapes.titre: Two sectors listed as natural environments
etapes.texte: The City is listing the parc-nature des Sources (38.32 ha) and the Anse-à-l'Orme sector of the Grand parc de l'Ouest (429 ha) in the Répertoire des milieux naturels protégés et contributifs à la biodiversité de l'agglomération, with conservation plans. It is also taking note of the 2025 report on the areas.

The City is awarding Gendron Gestion Civil inc. the contract to rebuild the culvert under chemin Senneville, as part of the modernization of the Bois-de-la-Roche agricultural hub, for a total expenditure of $481,850.45. The work includes the new culvert, roadway resurfacing and replacement of the safety guardrails.

aSurveiller.texte: Expected completion of work on the chemin de Senneville stone walls: July 10, 2026.
Filing of the Cap-Saint-Jacques lighting management plan: February 2027.
DarkSky International's response on the designation: April 2027.

itinerance.description: Support for organizations, warm-up spots and shelters for people experiencing homelessness.
itinerance.enBref: This year, the City is lending municipal buildings free of charge to organizations to open warm-up spots, and is funding organizations that work with people experiencing homelessness. It is also renewing a Ville-Marie public works team that carries out cleanliness work related to homelessness in other boroughs. In June, it set up a framework to accept private donations for housing and shelter projects.

etapes.texte: The City is lending three buildings free of charge to organizations for the 2025-2026 winter: the former church at 5600, 12e Avenue in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie to the Centre des Femmes de convictions de Montréal, the former monastery of the Recluses Missionnaires at 12050, boulevard Gouin Est to Projets Autochtones du Québec, and the former Bain St-Denis at 7075, rue Saint-Hubert to L'Amour en Action SYL DAN. All three loans end on April 30, 2026.

Verdun pays $12,950 to Société de développement social to keep two outreach workers in place from January 5 to February 6, 2026, in municipal facilities and their surrounding areas. Ahuntsic-Cartierville confirms the continuation of COHAB inc.'s contract to operate a warm-up spot during the 2025-2026 winter.

etapes.titre: Funding for organizations over three years
etapes.texte: The City grants $5,407,736 to 15 organizations and adds $3,942,461 to 10 already-funded organizations, under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs 2026-2028. The projects focus on the inclusion of people experiencing homelessness, cohabitation in public spaces, and awareness-raising.

etapes.titre: Public works team offered to boroughs
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie offers other boroughs the services of a public works team dedicated to cleanliness work related to homelessness, for 12 months starting in spring 2026, with a $931,328 budget for 2026 coming from the Service de la diversité et de l'inclusion sociale. Le Plateau-Mont-Royal, Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie, Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve and Le Sud-Ouest accept the offer.

Lachine, Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles and Ahuntsic-Cartierville in turn accept the Ville-Marie team; Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles' agreement runs from May 15, 2026 to May 15, 2027. City council adopts a declaration in support of people experiencing homelessness and in recognition of the organization Maison Mobile.

The City adopts a mechanism to govern private monetary donations for housing, shelter and social cohabitation projects for people experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness. Donors do not choose which project is funded, and the City may refuse a donation.

aSurveiller.texte: The agreement on the public works team with Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles runs until May 15, 2027.
Financial support under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs covers a three-year period ending on December 31, 2028.

louvain-est.description: The neighbourhood built on municipal land in Ahuntsic-Cartierville: acquisitions, soil decontamination, street names, temporary developments.

etapes.texte: City council approved the amendment of two leases for land south of rue de Louvain and west of boulevard Saint-Laurent. One serves as parking for Société de transport de Montréal employee vehicles, the other as paid parking for members of the clicknpark application.

The City is extending the free loan of a 10,000-square-foot lot to Ville en vert for its vegetable garden, a property subsidy valued at $121,100 (CM26 0447). City council also agreed to prepare, on its own, the lease with Îlot 84 for a 78,244-square-foot lot at the southeast corner of rue de Louvain Ouest and avenue de l'Esplanade, at no cost.

The Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough awarded Groupe MPotvin the redevelopment of rue de Louvain, between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum amount of $8,199,514.82 including taxes. The work covers sewers, water mains, lighting, traffic lights, sidewalks, the bike path and plantings.

etapes.titre: The central street gets a name
etapes.texte: City council named the new street at the heart of the Louvain eco-district "avenue des Solidarités." The name comes from a public call for proposals held in fall 2024 by the borough and the local heritage and toponymy committee.

etapes.titre: New street, networks and decontaminated soil
etapes.texte: The contract goes to Charex inc. to build an eco-district road with sewer, water main, roadway, lighting and environmental soil management, for a total expenditure of $15,366,336 including taxes. The City is adding a net $2,007,312.15, from the environmental liability reserve, to remediate the soil of the former gas station on the Louvain Est lot. A one-year free lease is also granted to the Laboratoire sur l'agriculture urbaine for sunflowers and a greenhouse.

aSurveiller.texte: The Esplanade - Louvain temporary space, at 150, rue de Louvain Ouest, is supported for the period from June 9 to December 31, 2026.
The Société de transport de Montréal parking lease begins on October 1, 2026, for three years, at a maximum of 92 days per year.
The land loan to the Laboratoire sur l'agriculture urbaine runs from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2027.
The Ville en vert vegetable garden can remain in place until December 31, 2027.
The rue de Louvain construction site between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel takes place in three phases, from May 2026 to August 2028.
Four other public spaces on the site remain to be named by the end of development, expected around 2032.

matieres-residuelles.description: Collections, sorting centres, biomethanation and ecocentres.
matieres-residuelles.enBref: The City changed collection schedules and frequencies in several boroughs, and extended contracts for food waste treatment, container collection, and container transport for the Saint-Laurent ecocentre. It also purchased collection bins, awarded companies hydro-excavation work with waste treatment, and received the 2025 waste management reports.

etapes.titre: Extensions of collection and treatment contracts
etapes.texte: The City extended by six months two contracts with Recyclage Notre-Dame inc. to treat food waste, with an additional expenditure of $3,269,055.43 taxes included [CG26 0045]. It also extended by 12 months the contracts for garbage collection in front-loading and semi-underground containers, and the contract for supplying and transporting containers for the Saint-Laurent ecocentre.

The executive committee changed the days, schedules and sectors for collection in L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève, Le Plateau-Mont-Royal and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve. In Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, garbage is collected every two weeks from November 1 to April 30 and every week from May 1 to October 31 [CE26 0466].

The City entered into agreements with USD Global inc., Orbis Canada ltée and Plasti-Bac inc. to supply and distribute collection bins for residents. Ahuntsic-Cartierville retained Ville en vert to inform and raise awareness among residents of buildings with eight units or fewer in the districts of Ahuntsic and Sault-au-Récollet, where garbage collection frequency is being changed, for $230,108.67 taxes included [CA26 09 0141].

Le Plateau-Mont-Royal authorized the removal of two dwelling units in the basement of 397, boulevard Saint-Joseph Ouest to set up a waste storage room of at least 28 m² and 32 bike spaces. Le Sud-Ouest lifted the requirement to set up a drop-off area on the site of the future building at 2380, rue Notre-Dame Ouest, and the executive committee approved an agreement with Tricentris, which is paying $43,773.61 for a program to loan reusable dishware, water fountains and sorting stations.

The urban agglomeration council took note of the 2025 waste management report and the accountability report for the 2020-2025 Master Plan: 415 kg of waste per person, 48% of materials diverted from disposal and 29 of the 49 actions completed [CG26 0311]. Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles, Saint-Laurent and Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce filed their expenditure reports for the activities delegated to them.

aSurveiller.texte: The extension of the food waste treatment contracts runs until September 30, 2026.
The container collection contracts and the Saint-Laurent ecocentre container contract are maintained until October 31, 2027.
The program to loan reusable dishware, water fountains and sorting stations is offered until December 31, 2026 at the latest.
The hydro-excavation contracts end on December 31, 2028.

namur-hippodrome.description: The new neighbourhood on the site of the former Blue Bonnets racetrack: sale of the lots, loan by-laws, waterworks for the Namur–De la Savane sector.

etapes.titre: More time to sell a lot
etapes.texte: The Québec government grants the City an extension until October 31, 2027 to sell a first lot on the site, west of boulevard Décarie and south of rue Paré. The postponement does not entail any financial compensation, and the other conditions of the 2017 transfer remain the same.

The City guarantees a $2,000,000 loan from the Canada Infrastructure Bank to Société GALOPH, a non-profit organization, to pay for feasibility studies for the residential project. On the same day, city council rejects a motion from the Official Opposition on governance and management of the neighbourhood's public assets.

City council adopts a $29,000,000 loan by-law for soil remediation, sewers and waterworks, street redevelopment, professional fees, and land purchases. This work must serve the first lots of phase 1, intended for social, community and affordable housing.

A second loan by-law, for $12,000,000, funds the construction of main water lines between boulevard Cavendish, in Saint-Laurent, and rue Isabella, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce. It covers plans and specifications, soil studies, surveying, decontamination, land purchases, and a first batch of work.

aSurveiller.texte: October 31, 2027: deadline given by the Québec government to sell a first lot on the site.
2031: the $128.3M federal grant is conditional on completing the infrastructure by this date.

parcs.description: Development and renovation of parks, including the Grand parc de l'Ouest.
parcs.enBref: The City is having parks redone across its territory: play areas, water play areas, trails, sports fields and dog parks. It awards design and construction contracts, adjusts contracts already underway, and pays for the decontamination of sites where parks will be developed. In the Grand parc de l'Ouest, it repairs structures, submits an application for an international designation and lists a sector in the directory of protected natural environments.

etapes.texte: The City entrusts the winning team of an architecture competition with the design of the bibliothèque Caroline-Dawson and the redevelopment of parc Le Prévost, in Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, for a total expenditure of $10,559,257.81, taxes included. It also pays $174,471.56 to Verdun for soil studies before redoing the play areas of parc Monseigneur-J.-A.-Richard, built on a former dump.

etapes.titre: Work and protection in the Grand parc de l'Ouest
etapes.texte: The City adds $162,897.98 to the contract for the renovation of the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville and awards a contract to rebuild a culvert under the same road, in the pôle agricole du Bois-de-la-Roche. It submits the application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector for the Urban Night Sky Place designation and lists the Anse-à-l'Orme sector in the directory of protected natural environments.

etapes.titre: Contracts for redevelopment of neighbourhood parks
etapes.texte: The boroughs award contracts to redo parks: parc à chien Lucie-Bruneau in Anjou, parc Mackenzie-King in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, parc canin Alexis-Nihon in Saint-Laurent, parc Monseigneur-Langlois in Verdun and parc Percy-Walters in Ville-Marie. Outremont pays $150,000 to redo the play module of parc-école Saint-Germain.

City council transfers a section of the former rue Eadie, measuring 810.2 m², to parc Campbell Ouest, in the Sud-Ouest. Le Plateau-Mont-Royal awards a construction contract for parc Denise-Morelle and pays a supplement to the project's architects, while LaSalle entrusts the redevelopment of parc J.O.R.-Leduc.

aSurveiller.texte: Parc des Eaux-Cachées public art competition: winner chosen in October 2026, contract in December 2026, installation of the artwork in 2028.
Urban Night Sky Place application: lighting plan submitted in February 2027, response from DarkSky expected in April 2027, site compliance work in April 2032.
Parc du Bassin-à-Bois: final acceptance of the work expected in June 2027.
Parc Denise-Morelle: work from early August 2026 to November 2026.
Parc J.O.R.-Leduc: work from August 2026 to June 2028.
Parc Percy-Walters: work from July to November 2026, with a continuation in spring 2027.

pietonnisation.description: Pedestrian streets, public squares and business promotion ordinances.
pietonnisation.enBref: This year, the City and the boroughs are organizing the pedestrian streets for summer 2026: funding for boroughs and business development corporations, followed by ordinances that close streets to cars and regulate terraces, sales, music and signage. Temporary public squares are also being set up, and support services are being added, such as on-demand transit on avenue du Mont-Royal.

etapes.titre: Grant framework and end of a lawsuit
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie adopts a by-law allowing it to subsidize its business development corporations to pedestrianize streets in 2026, up to $425 per linear metre. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie settles out of court for $41,686.46 a lawsuit related to work on the public square at the corner of rue Beaubien Est and rue Boyer.

The executive committee pays $2,694,500 to six boroughs for pedestrian streets on commercial arteries. Ville-Marie and Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce adopt their first ordinances, including the Placette CDN, open from April 1 to October 31, 2026.

Ville-Marie grants $375,500 to the Société de développement commercial du Village for rue Sainte-Catherine Est, and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension $102,045 for rue Villeray. Outremont sets aside $105,000 for avenue Bernard, in addition to a $106,000 grant from the Service du développement économique.

Outremont closes avenue Bernard from May 19 to September 24, 2026. Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce turns avenue Royal and avenue Madison into pedestrian streets and public squares from June 1 to October 31, 2026. Ville-Marie adjusts the dates of three pedestrianizations.

Le Plateau-Mont-Royal bans amplified instruments and games between 9 p.m. and 8 a.m. on pedestrianized avenues. The City pays $40,000 to animate the rue Notre-Dame Ouest pedestrian street from July 10 to 19, 2026, and Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce authorizes a business promotion on avenue de Monkland.

aSurveiller.texte: Activities on the rue Notre-Dame Ouest pedestrian street from July 10 to 19, 2026; the organization must submit its accountability report by August 31, 2026 at the latest.
Avenue de Monkland closed to traffic from August 19 at 10 p.m. to August 24 at 7 a.m., with activities from August 20 to 23, 2026.
Avenue Lacombe closed to cars from September 10 to 13, 2026.
Rue Ontario Est pedestrianized until September 18, 2026; parking meters return on September 17, 2026.
Avenue Bernard fully reopened to traffic as of September 25, 2026.
Placette CDN and avenues Royal and Madison: traffic returns after October 31, 2026, namely November 1, 2026 for the placette.

plan-urbanisme.description: The PUM and the concordance by-laws each borough adopts to comply with it.

etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville amended its urban planning by-law regarding the planting, maintenance, protection and felling of trees. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie revised three by-laws, and Saint-Léonard two, following public consultations held on February 26 and February 11, 2026.

The borough changed the heights, uses and lot coverage rate in the sector bounded by avenues Papineau, Émile-Journault and André-Grasset and rue Legendre Est. It also increased the permitted heights on sections of rue Lajeunesse, between boulevards Crémazie and Henri-Bourassa, to follow the Plan's density rules.

Following the public consultation of March 25, 2026, the borough adopted a by-law covering urban planning, special projects, demolition, authorization certificates and cadastral operations. The text allows a maximum height of 103 m on the block of the former terrasse Peel and permits public transit stations in category E.1 sectors.

etapes.titre: Requests for extension to the ministry
etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville requested twelve more months, until June 16, 2027, to adopt its concordance by-laws. L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève requested six more months, citing staff shortages, the complexity of its territory and the fall 2025 election.

aSurveiller.texte: Mid-June 2026: L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève plans to present its project to elected officials, then hold a public consultation in September or October 2026.
June 16, 2027: deadline set by the ministry for Saint-Léonard to adopt all its concordance by-laws; Ahuntsic-Cartierville requested the same deadline.
June 17, 2027: deadline given to Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension to update its by-laws; its zoning by-law must be replaced in 2027.

securite-publique.description: The City of Montréal's police department (Service de police de la Ville de Montréal): contracts, neighbourhood police stations, city council motions.
securite-publique.enBref: The City funds and equips the Service de police de la Ville de Montréal: a loan for specialized equipment, the purchase of motorcycles and ammunition, service contracts for its buildings and its IT system. It also renews leases for neighbourhood police stations and SPVM premises, and lends police officers to the Gendarmerie royale du Canada and the Sûreté du Québec. Some borough councils receive reports from neighbourhood police station 7 and adopt motions of support for the SPVM.

etapes.texte: The City is purchasing patrol motorcycles for a total expense of $550,899.04, taxes included, and is entering into an agreement for the supply of 9 mm practice ammunition used for firearms training. It is also accepting an $8,000 grant from the Department of Justice of Canada for an information campaign on sexual assault during National Victims and Survivors of Crime Week, from May 11 to 15, 2026.

The City is extending housekeeping services for headquarters, mail courier services, and maintenance of the computer-assisted dispatch system software. It is also awarding a contract for meals for detained persons and agreements for carpentry and painting services in SPVM buildings.

aSurveiller.texte: Neighbourhood police station 46's "Fèves au lard" fundraising day is held on October 23, 2026.
The extension of the dispatch system software maintenance contract runs until May 4, 2027.
The work to replace the oil heating in the cavalry building must be completed by September 30, 2027.
The contract for meals for detained persons runs until April 30, 2029, with a 12-month extension option.

transport-collectif.description: What the City decides about the transit network: land sold to the STM, areas around stations, agreements.
transport-collectif.enBref: This year, the City approved the budget and capital works program of the Société de transport de Montréal (STM), then a loan by-law for the corporation. It also sold or leased land to the STM to expand métro facilities, entrusted the STM with work related to the blue line extension, and regulated work sites in the métro tunnel. It also signed a letter of non-objection for the reconstruction of a bridge-tunnel above the REM.

etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration council adopted the STM's 2026 budget, balanced at $1,804,314,410 in revenues and expenditures alike, and the 2026-2035 capital works program. City council gave the same direction.

The City entered into a 36-month agreement with Produits Suncor Énergie for clear diesel and diesel containing renewable fuel, following a call for tenders by the STM. It also purchased, without a call for tenders, advertising space from Astral Affichage in the métro and buses for Espace pour la vie, up to $172,462.50 including taxes.

The City is leasing to the STM a 2,787-square-metre lot in Ahuntsic-Cartierville, south of rue de Louvain, as parking for vehicles of officers with a permit sticker, for a total rent of $49,293. The same borough modified bus waiting posts within its territory as part of the network overhaul.

The City signed an agreement with the STM to build a pavilion in Parc Irma-LeVasseur, adjoining the métro ventilation station on avenue Wiseman, in Outremont. It also entrusted the STM with carrying out its municipal work at the future Pie-IX and Viau stations, on rue Jean-Talon Est, for an expenditure of $3,808,451.29 including taxes.

etapes.titre: Décarie lot and tunnel work site
etapes.texte: Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce signed a new access agreement with the STM for a vacant 3,274.2-square-metre lot at 4636-4670, boulevard Décarie, and terminated the 2024 transitional occupancy agreement. Ville-Marie authorized the STM to drill and rehabilitate the vault of the green line tunnel, between Berri-UQAM and Saint-Laurent, 24 hours a day.

aSurveiller.texte: Drilling and rehabilitation work on the green line tunnel vault until July 31, 2026.
Awarding of contracts for the Pie-IX and Viau stations in August and October 2026; opening of the blue line extension stations expected in 2031.
Start of the STM's parking lease on October 1, 2026, for three years, at a rate of 92 days per year.
Work on the Rielle ventilation station, in Verdun, until December 2027.
Complete closure of rue Wilderton, for a maximum of two weeks, during the 2027 summer vacation period; bridge-tunnel reconstruction work from June 2026 to March 2028.

velo.titre: Bikes: REV, bike paths, and BIXI
velo.description: The Réseau express vélo, bike paths and bike lanes, and the self-service bike system.
velo.enBref: This year, the City is buying bikes, docks, and station parts for the BIXI system, and having new stations installed at street work sites. It is also funding the repair of existing bike lanes, including the REV Lajeunesse, and formalizing the rent for Hydro-Québec lands crossed by bike paths. Boroughs, for their part, oversee the development and maintenance of their bike lanes.

etapes.texte: Outremont approves spending of $100,000, taxes included, for concrete, de-icing salt, and abrasives intended in particular for bike paths. Ahuntsic-Cartierville awards Déneigement et Excavation M. Gauthier inc. the rental of a mini sweeper with operator for spring cleaning of paths less than 1.8 metres wide, for $153,395.05, taxes included.

etapes.titre: Sustainable mobility corridors in the east end
etapes.texte: City council adds $3,400,000, taxes included, to the contract with Bruneau Électrique inc. for traffic lights, civil and electrical work, and bike paths in Ville-Marie and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, on rue Hochelaga and rue du Havre. The contract reaches $11,399,999.99, taxes included.

etapes.titre: Hydro-Québec lands under the bike paths
etapes.texte: City council approves a $125,167.62 agreement, taxes included, with Hydro-Québec for rents from 2014 to 2025 on 19 lands used for bike paths, parks, and community gardens. It then approves a 10-year lease, at a total rent of $46,896, taxes included, to lease about 366 square metres in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles for bike path purposes.

etapes.titre: Repair of the REV Lajeunesse and rue Lajoie
etapes.texte: Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension offers to take charge of the repair of sections of the REV Lajeunesse, between rue Jarry and boulevard Crémazie, and city council accepts this offer as well as one from Ville-Marie for roadway and bike path work under the Plan Vélo 2019. Outremont tables a draft by-law to convert the shared lane on avenue Lajoie, between Stuart and Outremont, into a one-way bike path.

aSurveiller.texte: For the REV Lajeunesse, the file indicates a call for tenders in May 2026, contracts awarded in June, and work from July to August 2026.
The UCI Road World Championships are held in Montréal from September 20 to 27, 2026; sections along the route are targeted by roadway work in Ville-Marie.
The repair of the bike lane on rue De Louvain, between west of rue d'Iberville and boulevard Saint-Michel, is listed at $570,000 in 2027.
Work on the sustainable mobility corridors resumes in spring 2026, for completion in spring or summer 2026.
